script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Sci-Fi
Theme: identity

Begin screenplay.

Title: The Shape Shifter's Lament

INT. LABORATORY - NIGHT

DR. ELLIOT MORGAN, a brilliant but eccentric scientist, sits in front of a holographic computer console, surrounded by test tubes, beakers, and scientific equipment. He wears glasses and a lab coat with stains of various colors. His eyes are focused on the hologram, which displays a complex equation.

ELLIOT (V.O.)
(sighs) I'm so close. The key to human identity lies within the very building blocks of life. But how do I prove it?

Suddenly, a blinding light engulfs the laboratory, and Elliot's body transforms into a pool of liquid. He watches in awe as the substance takes on the shape of a beautiful woman. She is ADRIA, a woman from Elliot's past.

ADRIA
(smiling) You always were a brilliant scientist, Elliot. But your experiments, they come with a price.

ELLIOT
(startled) Adria? Is this some kind of hallucination?

ADRIA
No, my love. It's the truth of who you really are. Your identity is not confined to your physical form. It's your thoughts, your memories, your emotions. And with this power, you can experience them all.

EXT. CITY PARK - DAY

Elliot, now in the form of Adria, walks through the park, observing the world around her. Children play, couples stroll, and birds chirp. She reaches out to touch a tree, her fingers passing through the bark.

ADRIA (V.O.)
(whispers) The world is so much more beautiful when you're not confined by your own flesh.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Elliot, now transformed into an elderly man, sits at a table in a bustling coffee shop. He watches as a young woman, LUCY, enters and orders a latte. He remembers their past conversations, their shared laughter.

ELDERLY ELLLIOT
(to himself) I cannot change the past, but maybe I can make amends.

Lucy sits down across from him. She's startled when she recognizes him but quickly composes herself.

LUCY
(smiling) Elliot, is it really you?

ELLIOT
(nods) Yes, it's me. And I have something I'd like to tell you.

INT. LABORATORY - NIGHT

Elliot, back in his original form, stands before the holographic console, surrounded by the remnants of his shattered experiments. He looks at Adria, who stands next to him, a sad expression on her face.

ADRIA
You've caused so much damage, Elliot. But you've also experienced the depths of human emotion. You've walked in the shoes of the young and the old, the rich and the poor. You've touched the lives of so many, even if only for a moment.

ELLIOT
(sighs) But at what cost?

ADRIA
The cost of true understanding, Elliot. The cost of knowing who you really are.

ELLIOT
(determined) Then I will continue my work. I will find a way to control this power, to use it for the betterment of mankind.

ADRIA
(nods) I believe in you, Elliot.

INT. LABORATORY - DAY

Elliot, now transformed into a brilliant artist, paints a scene of the city park, capturing the essence of life in every stroke. He smiles as he creates a work of art that speaks to the very core of what it means to be human.

FADE OUT.

End screenplay.
